&nbsp;

::: {.alert .alert-info}

This article shows how to customize dynamic spectrograms, layer by layer. The [main vignette](dynaSpec.html) shows the basic usage of each layer. As there, the examples create interactive web pages: press play to watch the spectrogram along with the sound, click on it to play from that point, and use the speed slider to slow the sound down. Use `save_dynaspec()` with a file name ending in `.mp4` to create videos instead.

:::

```{r}
library(dynaSpec)
library(viridis)
library(seewave)

data("canyon_wren")
```

Some examples use recordings from the package [NatureSounds](https://cran.r-project.org/package=NatureSounds) or downloaded from the web (sounds must be 'Wave' objects or local '.wav' or '.mp3' files, so recordings are downloaded first).

Layers can be stored in an object and modified by adding more layers. Arguments of `spectrogram()`, `dynatheme()` and style layers are combined with the previous ones (so only the settings that change need to be supplied), while other panel and player layers replace previous ones of the same kind, and selections and captions are added. Settings not supplied take the defaults of each style.

# Spectrograms

`spectrogram()` sets how the spectrogram is computed (window length `wl`, overlap `ovlp`, window function `wn`) and drawn (color palette `pal`, amplitude levels of the colors `collevels`, background `colbg`). Other arguments are passed to `seewave::spectro()`:

```{r}
wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300)

# palette and amplitude range
wren + spectrogram(pal = mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1))
```

Black and white spectrogram with a wider amplitude range (fainter sounds are shown):

```{r}
wren + spectrogram(pal = reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 5))
```

A black background:

```{r}
wren + spectrogram(pal = viridis, colbg = "black")
```

In paged spectrograms the palette can also be the name of a 'viridis' palette (e.g. "magma") or two colors for a gradient, and `amp.trans` brightens the spectrogram (a nonlinear transformation that collapses the difference between loud and quiet sounds; 1 means no transformation):

```{r}
f <- list.files(system.file(package = "dynaSpec"), pattern = "\\.wav$", full.names = TRUE)

swallow <- dynaspec(f[1]) +
  spectrogram(amp.trans = 3, collevels = seq(-35, 0, 1)) +
  paged() +
  dynatheme(axis.type = "standard")

swallow
```

# Panels

Oscillograms and amplitude envelopes can go above or below the spectrogram (`position`), with their own color (`col`) and height relative to the spectrogram (`height`). Power spectra go on the left or right side (`side`), with a given width (`width`, as a proportion of the figure):

```{r}
cols <- mako(10)

wren +
  spectrogram(pal = mako, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)) +
  oscillogram(position = "above", col = cols[3], height = 0.3) +
  envelope(col = cols[5], height = 0.3) +
  spectrum(side = "left", col = cols[5], width = 0.12)
```

With several rows each row shows its own power spectrum, on the same scale:

```{r}
wren +
  spectrum(col = cols[5]) +
  static(rows = 2, height = 350)
```

In scrolling spectrograms the lower panel can be an overview of the whole sound (`overview()`, with its relative `height`), an oscillogram or an envelope:

```{r}
wren +
  envelope(col = cols[5]) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7)
```

# Themes

`dynatheme()` sets the look of all styles: axis titles (`xlab`, `ylab`), the size of titles and labels (`cex.lab`, `cex.axis`), the font of titles (`font.lab`), the color of axes and text (`col.lab`), the type of axes (`axis.type`) and the background around the panels (`bg`):

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram() +
  dynatheme(xlab = "Tiempo (s)", ylab = "Frecuencia (kHz)", cex.lab = 1.4, font.lab = 2, col.lab = "gray30")
```

It also sets the font family of all text (`family`), the orientation of frequency labels (`las`), the length of ticks (`tick.length`), boxes around panels (`box`, `col.box`), grid lines (`grid`, `col.grid`), the background of oscillogram, envelope and spectrum panels (`col.panel`) and the color and size of titles (`col.title`, `cex.title`):

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram() +
  spectrum() +
  dynatheme(family = "serif", las = 1, tick.length = 0.3, box = FALSE, grid = TRUE, col.panel = "gray95")
```

Themes can also set the colors of the plot: the spectrogram palette and background (`pal`, `colbg`), the color of oscillograms, envelopes and spectra (`col.wave`), the play line (`col.line`) and the highlight box of paged spectrograms (`col.highlight`). These are used when they are not supplied in the other layers (e.g. `spectrogram(pal = )` takes precedence). `col.bar` and `bg.bar` set the colors of the player controls of web pages. A dark theme:

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram() +
  dynatheme(bg = "black", col.lab = "white", pal = viridis, colbg = "black", col.wave = viridis(10)[7], col.line = "white",
            col.bar = "white", bg.bar = "black")
```

## Preset themes

Preset themes set several settings at once: `dynatheme_dark()`, `dynatheme_presentation()` (large bold text for slides), `dynatheme_paper()` (black and white with serif fonts, for printed figures), `dynatheme_minimal()` (no boxes and light gray axes), `dynatheme_transparent()` (transparent background, to blend in slides or web pages of any color) and `dynatheme_void()` (no axes or boxes). Their settings can be changed in the call, or by adding `dynatheme()` afterwards (adding a preset replaces previous themes):

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram() +
  envelope() +
  dynatheme_dark(cex.lab = 1.3) +
  player(buttons = c("time", "loop", "volume"))
```

```{r}
wren +
  oscillogram() +
  dynatheme_paper()
```

```{r}
wren +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7) +
  dynatheme_presentation()
```

`axis.type` can be "standard", "none" or, in scrolling spectrograms, "minimal" (1 s and 1 kHz scale bars):

```{r}
wren +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7) +
  dynatheme(axis.type = "minimal")
```

# Static spectrograms

`static()` sets the color of the play line and active buttons (`lcol`), the size and resolution of each row (`width`, `height`, in pixels, and `res`), the number of rows (`rows`), whether the play line is shown (`play.line`) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`):

```{r}
wren +
  static(lcol = "#E69F00", width = 1200, height = 400, res = 120)
```

Without the moving line (clicking on the figure still plays the sound from that point):

```{r}
wren + static(play.line = FALSE)
```

# Scrolling spectrograms

`scrolling()` sets the time window shown (`t.display`), whether the time axis moves along with the spectrogram (`fix.time = FALSE`), the play line (`lcol`, `lty`, `lwd`), the initial speed (`speed`), a delay before the spectrogram starts moving (`buffer`, in s), looping (`loop`), the size and resolution of the frames (`width`, `height`, `res`) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`):

```{r}
wren +
  spectrogram(pal = viridis, colbg = "black") +
  oscillogram(col = "#31688E99") +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7, fix.time = FALSE, speed = 0.5, lcol = "white", lty = 1, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120)
```

Long-billed hermit song at 1/5 speed, without axes and looping (web pages loop until paused):

```{r}
data("Phae.long4", package = "NatureSounds")

dynaspec(Phae.long4, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300, ovlp = 90, pal = magma, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 5), colbg = "black") +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120, speed = 0.2, loop = 3) +
  dynatheme(axis.type = "none")
```

The first 20 s of a northern nightingale wren recording from [xeno-canto](https://www.xeno-canto.org) using a custom color palette:

```{r}
nightingale_wren <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file("https://xeno-canto.org/518334/download", nightingale_wren, mode = "wb")

custom_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#2d2d86", "#2d2d86", reverse.terrain.colors(10)[5:10]))

dynaspec(nightingale_wren, flim = c(2, 8), crop = 20) +
  spectrogram(wl = 600, ovlp = 95, pal = custom_pal, collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5), colbg = "#2d2d86") +
  scrolling(t.display = 3, width = 700, height = 250, res = 100, lcol = "#FFFFFFE6")
```

Spix's disc-winged bat inquiry call slowed down 16 times (`speed = 0.0625`, the slowest speed web browsers can play):

```{r}
data("thyroptera.est", package = "NatureSounds")

# extract one call
thy_wav <- attributes(thyroptera.est)$wave.objects[[12]]

# convert to 16 bits (as the silence added below)
thy_wav <- tuneR::normalize(thy_wav, unit = "16")

# add silence at both sides
thy_wav <- pastew(tuneR::silence(duration = 0.05, samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate, xunit = "time"),
                  thy_wav, output = "Wave")
thy_wav <- pastew(thy_wav, tuneR::silence(duration = 0.04, samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate, xunit = "time"),
                  output = "Wave")

dynaspec(thy_wav, flim = c(12, 37)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 400, ovlp = 95, pal = inferno, collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5), colbg = "black") +
  oscillogram(col = inferno(10, alpha = 0.9)[3]) +
  scrolling(t.display = 0.08, width = 700, height = 250, res = 100, lcol = "#FFFFFFE6", lty = 1,
            speed = 0.0625, loop = 4)
```

Other options of `scrolling()` are a custom spectrogram function (`spectro.call`, a call made with `base::call()`), spectral derivatives (`derivative = TRUE`, requires the package 'imager') and the window length in ms (`hop.size`).

# Paged spectrograms

`paged()` sets the duration of each page (`t.display`), the highlight box (`highlight.col`, `highlight.alpha`), the cursor (`lcol`), a title (`title`), an amplitude color scale (`plot.legend = TRUE`), the size of the pages (`spec.width`, `spec.height`, in inches) and the frames per second of videos (`fps`). Other arguments set the preparation of the pages (e.g. `resample.rate`, `amp.thresh` or `filter`):

```{r}
swallow +
  paged(title = "Female barn swallow", highlight.col = "#2d2d86", highlight.alpha = 0.4, lcol = "#FFEA46") +
  dynatheme(bg = "black")
```

The first 12 s of a humpback whale song, with 3 s pages and the frequency range used by these whales (0-700 Hz):

```{r}
whale <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file("http://www.oceanmammalinst.org/songs/hmpback3.wav", whale, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(whale, flim = c(0, 0.7), crop = 12) +
  spectrogram(amp.trans = 3) +
  paged(t.display = 3)
```

A common nighthawk call from [xeno-canto](https://www.xeno-canto.org) with a two-color palette:

```{r}
nighthawk <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file("https://xeno-canto.org/490771/download", nighthawk, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(nighthawk, crop = 20) +
  spectrogram(pal = c("white", "black")) +
  paged(t.display = 4, highlight.col = "#d1b0ff", lcol = "#7817ff")
```

# Selections

`selections()` takes the colors (`col`, a color or the name of a column of the selection table) and labels (`labels`, the name of a column) of the boxes from the selection table, along with their opacity (`alpha`), borders (`border`, `lwd`), the size of the labels (`cex`) and whether boxes span only the frequency range of the selections (`freq`). The following code highlights the male and female parts of a house wren duet (after downloading the recording and selection table from GitHub):

```{r}
# house wren male-female duet recording
hs_wren <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file("https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/house_wren_male_female_duet.wav",
              hs_wren, mode = "wb")

# and selection table
st <- read.csv("https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/house_wren_male_female_duet.csv")

# colors and labels
st$colors <- viridis(10)[c(3, 8)]
st$labels <- c("male", "female")

duet <- dynaspec(hs_wren, flim = c(1, 13)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 512, pal = reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 1)) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.2, loop = 3, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120)

duet + selections(st, col = "colors", alpha = 0.4, labels = "labels", cex = 1.5)
```

With box borders, spanning the whole frequency range (`freq = FALSE`), and an oscillogram:

```{r}
duet +
  selections(st, col = "colors", alpha = 0.3, border = "gray30", lwd = 2, freq = FALSE) +
  oscillogram()
```

Selection tables made with [warbleR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=warbleR) can be used directly. When they have selections of several sound files, only those of the sound shown are used (matching the file name), or the sound file is chosen with `sound.file` (e.g. for 'Wave' objects):

```{r}
data("lbh_selec_table", package = "warbleR")
data("Phae.long1", package = "NatureSounds")

dynaspec(Phae.long1, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300) +
  selections(lbh_selec_table, sound.file = "Phae.long1.wav", labels = "selec")
```

# Captions

`captions()` adds text at a fixed position of the figure (`x` and `y`, as proportions of the figure width and height), shown during a time range of the sound (`start` and `end`, in s). `fading` adds fade-in and fade-out effects (in s), and `col`, `cex` and `font` set the color, size and font. Several captions can be shown one after the other, and several caption layers can be added at different positions. The following code labels the frog species calling in a recording from Costa Rica:

```{r}
# frog recording from GitHub
frogs <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file("https://github.com/maRce10/example_sounds/raw/refs/heads/main/CostaRican_frogs.wav",
              frogs, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(frogs, flim = c(0, 5.5), crop = c(35.3, 50.5)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 512, ovlp = 95, pal = cividis, collevels = seq(-60, 0, 5), colbg = "black") +
  oscillogram(col = "#31688E", height = 1 / 3) +
  captions(
    c("Dendropsophus ebraccatus", "Eleutherodactylus coqui"),
    start = c(35.7, 42.3),
    end = c(40.8, 50.1),
    x = 0.3,
    y = 0.9,
    col = "#FFEA46CC",
    font = 3,
    fading = 0.6
  ) +
  captions("Costa Rica", start = 35.3, end = 50.5, x = 0.9, y = 0.9, col = "white", cex = 0.8) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.1, loop = 3, width = 1200, height = 550, res = 200, lcol = "#FFFFFFCC", lty = 3) +
  dynatheme(bg = "black", col.lab = "white")
```

Note that times of selections and captions refer to the original recording, even when it is cropped (`crop`).

# Player

`player()` sets the speeds offered by the speed slider of web pages (the first one is the initial speed; a single speed hides the slider), whether the pitch is kept when slowing down by default and the additional controls shown (`buttons`). A player with only the play button, for instance to embed in a presentation:

```{r}
wren + player(speeds = 1, buttons = character())
```

A player with all controls, starting at half speed and looping (the loop button starts pressed when `scrolling(loop)` is larger than 1):

```{r}
wren +
  player(speeds = c(0.5, 1, 0.25), buttons = c("time", "loop", "volume", "download", "fullscreen")) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7, loop = 2)
```

The download button saves the sound embedded in the web page (named after the sound file or 'Wave' object), and the full screen button enlarges the player to the size of the screen (e.g. for presentations; web browsers may not allow full screen in embedded frames).

# Videos

Videos (`save_dynaspec()` with a file name ending in `.mp4`) use the same settings as web pages. Videos of scrolling spectrograms render every frame, which can be sped up by using several cores (`parallel`) and lowering the frames per second (`fps`):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
save_dynaspec(duet + scrolling(parallel = 4, fps = 30), "house_wren_duet.mp4")
```
